question: After the pacing blocker is fixed, should outbound recovery keep ambiguous rows pending with backoff when no reconciliation-capable adapter is available, or keep current main's fail-closed terminalization until the broader delivery ledger exists?
rationale: Both outcomes are defensible: pending preserves future recoverability, while fail-closed gives clearer operator state; tests can prove mechanics but not the preferred product/operations tradeoff.

options.title: Accept recoverable pending
options.body: Merge the mitigation after the no-op pacing repair and green exact-head checks, while leaving full operator surfacing and reconciliation design to the canonical issue.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Pause or close this PR and keep ambiguous no-adapter rows terminal until maintainers design the broader delivery ledger.

options.title: Require operator surfacing first
options.body: Ask for a doctor, UI, or API surface before making ambiguous rows remain pending longer.

recommendation.title: Accept recoverable pending
recommendation.body: Merge the mitigation after the no-op pacing repair and green exact-head checks, while leaving full operator surfacing and reconciliation design to the canonical issue.
